notes: network_allowed: HTTP happens ONLY in a declared provider adapter (ollama_client, mistral_client, openrouter_client, and custom_endpoint, which is the ONE parameterised adapter for user-supplied OpenAI-compatible servers rather than a per-server module) or a declared server/demo module; everything else asks the directory. Amended 2026-08-24: the rule was written when one provider existed and said 'the ONE place'. Provider plurality is now a requirement, not a convenience — a single provider's 429 stopped a whole campaign — so the invariant is 'only in a declared adapter', and each adapter is listed above. Adding a provider means adding its adapter here with its reason, never relaxing the rule.

subprocess_allowed: opencode_client (declared tool adapter), smoke_ladder.submit_to_kaggle (declared external effect, explicit call sites only), and _conformance_scan.scan_min_python_syntax, which must invoke an OLDER interpreter to check syntax the current one accepts — a 3.14 workstation cannot detect PEP 701 usage that breaks the declared 3.10 floor, and that shipped once.
eval/exec: never — logic_ast interprets a closed operator set instead.
dynamic imports: registry/self-test plumbing only; a dynamic import elsewhere is a registration bypass.
secret patterns scan code AND receipts — evidence files must be secret-free too.

module_size_exceptions.loop/kernel.py: the nine-step executor's default implementations; split plan: move per-step defaults into loop/steps/ facades one step at a time
module_size_exceptions.loop/recursive_loop.py: the canonical Loop runtime; split plan: extract LoopSpec/pause-resume into loop/spec.py once the kernel routes through run_next_iteration

suite_collection_exceptions.static_architecture/ollama_client.py: its self_test makes LIVE provider calls; folding it would make the suite non-deterministic and bill a provider on every run. Exercised by the dated live-mode canary receipt instead.
suite_collection_exceptions.static_architecture/event_vocabulary.py: no self_test of its own: it was split out of chronicle.py at the size cap and every one of its behaviours is exercised by chronicle.self_test (closed vocabulary, total projection, coverage honesty, adversarial undeclared-family refusal). A duplicate suite would test the same code twice and drift.

resource_envelope_modules.loop/intelligence_loops.py: IS the loop envelope for the four intelligence pillars — wrapping a store record into a loop requires reaching the store. The envelope's own body is the base case for that boundary, not a crossing of it.
resource_envelope_modules.loop/recursive_loop.py: the runtime kernel: committing a run's own Chronicle is the machinery that executes the loop abstraction, not a product-level caller reaching past it.
resource_envelope_modules.static_architecture/retrieval.py: the search substrate itself — the Retriever reading the store it ranks is surface-internal, the same class as a surface calling itself.
resource_envelope_modules.loop/loop_capsule.py: IS the ref/capsule layer: turning a store row into a LoopRef requires reading the row. The layer that creates the boundary is the base case for it, not a crossing of it.

direct_resource_access_note: ZERO-TOLERANCE as of 2026-08-24. The rule graduated from a ratchet: every product-level direct resource access was routed through its loop envelope, so the baseline is 0 and any new one fails the build. Do not raise this to make a build pass — route the call through a loop.

boundary_register_exempt_modules.static_architecture/reasoning_call.py: the CALLER that crosses the model-invocation boundary, which is already a register row (envelope: as_model_loop). It owns no separate boundary of its own.
boundary_register_exempt_modules.code_nodes/guided_setup.py: the first-run WALKTHROUGH: it orchestrates existing boundaries (the practitioner envelope, provider discovery, the knowledge loader) and owns none of them. Every envelope it calls is already a register row; adding a second row for the caller would claim ownership it does not have.
boundary_register_exempt_modules.code_nodes/universal_solve.py: the ROUTING front door: it orients on a task and dispatches to an executor that owns the boundary, using the practitioner envelope only as a caller when no executor fits the modality. Every envelope it touches is already a register row; a second row would claim ownership it does not have.
boundary_register_exempt_modules.code_nodes/public_examples.py: installed examples orchestrate existing practitioner, report, and intelligence boundaries for teaching. They own no new boundary; registering them would duplicate the envelopes they demonstrate.

dynamic_import_allowed_modules_reasons.__init__.py: the package's documented public surface (from loop_engine import PractitionerLoop) resolved LAZILY, so importing the package stays cheap and no import cycle is created. This is a re-export of the canonical runtime, NOT the registration bypass the gate exists to catch: it registers nothing, and every name resolves to an already-mapped module.
